title: 4 Stocks You’ll Wish You Bought on This Dip (One Is Down Over 50%)
creator: MarketBeat
summary: MarketBeat host Bridget talks buy-the-dip ideas with guest Alec Green, chief investment strategist at the Oxford Club. Green sees a concentrated market (top 8 S&P names >35% of the index) leaving overlooked mid/large and international names cheap despite strong earnings, with the post-midterm 'midterm miracle' seasonality (~+19.5% average over the following 9 months) as a near-term catalyst. His four picks: MercadoLibre (MELI), Novo Nordisk (NVO, recently re-added at under 10x earnings), Tyler Technologies (TYL) and speculative Summit Therapeutics (SMMT, FDA decision due mid-November).

calls.video_title: 4 Stocks You’ll Wish You Bought on This Dip (One Is Down Over 50%)
calls.thesis: BUY (first tracked for MarketBeat; guest Alec Green, Oxford Club) — MercadoLibre, the 'Amazon of Latin America', dominates LatAm e-commerce more than Amazon dominates the US; recent margin concerns are overdone because spend was for long-term growth; long-term uptrend intact and stock undervalued on forward sales/earnings. No price stated.
calls.bull_case: LatAm e-commerce penetration still early (smartphone/computer ownership lower, fragmented retail); sales and earnings growth ahead should drive sharp appreciation.
calls.bear_case: Margin pressure from long-term growth spending dented short-term results; holders over the past year are slightly underwater.

calls.thesis: BUY (first tracked for MarketBeat; guest Alec Green) — Novo Nordisk recently re-added to his portfolio after a prior 123% gain; Wegovy GLP-1 market is just getting started, stock trades at under 10x earnings with a big dividend yield, and earnings likely to beat expectations. No share price stated.
calls.bull_case: GLP-1 use expands (only ~10% of Americans on them), insurance/government coverage grows, pipeline approvals add upside, and users must stay on the drug to keep weight off.
calls.bear_case: Repeated earnings misses drove the downtrend; Eli Lilly is the current GLP-1 leader and keeps improving its competing drugs.

calls.thesis: BUY (first tracked for MarketBeat; guest Alec Green) — Tyler Technologies sells efficiency software to governments; contracts are extremely sticky, earnings are stable and trending up, and the SaaS sell-off on AI-replacement fears was overblown — AI augments rather than replaces its work. No price stated.

calls.price_at_call: under $15 (stated); traded as high as ~$33 in the last ~18 months
calls.thesis: BUY, speculative / small position only (first tracked for MarketBeat; guest Alec Green) — Summit Therapeutics (captions say 'Summit Technologies') is a pre-revenue China-based biotech whose lung-cancer drug beat expectations in Chinese tests; FDA decision expected mid-November (~14-15 Nov) on US use vs Merck's Keytruda, plus Q4 China trial results; he suggests a small position and even November calls, taking at least half off on a big pop.
calls.bull_case: FDA approval could produce a big spike / 'moonshot'; Baker Brothers hold a large position.
calls.bear_case: Pre-revenue and highly volatile; if FDA approval fails, the thesis and any November calls fail with it.
